evidence: unreadable: In seg2:end the label 'Frozen in permafrost soil 1700B' is printed on top of 'Earth's whole atmosphere 870B', and both garble into an overlapping mess.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg2:end shows the pink label 'Frozen in permafrost soil 1700B' drawn straight over the white 'Earth's whole atmosphere 870B' at the same y, so neither can be read. In seg2:mid the two posts are thin lines barely taller than each other, even though 1700 is almost double 870.
weakest_scene.root_cause: Both series labels are anchored at the same left-side height instead of each sitting on its own post. The posts are also hairline poles that never show the near-doubling, so the scene relies on text, and that text collides.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Put each label directly above its own post, with no shared baseline, and keep them at least one line-height apart. Make the two quantities volumes whose heights really sit at 870 vs 1700, for example a frozen soil block twice as tall as an atmosphere block, so the near-doubling is visible without reading. Have Data pull the measuring tape from the top of one to the top of the other while the gap label lands.
